title: Max Pooling Forward and Backward
signature: def maxpool(x, dout, pool_h, pool_w, stride) -> tuple
hints: Max is a router: in the backward pass, the whole upstream gradient of a window goes to the single position that won.
np.argmax returns the FIRST maximum in row-major order, which is exactly the tie rule you need. Flatten each window to length pool_h * pool_w first.
Windows overlap when stride < pool size, so one pixel can win several windows. Add (+=) its gradients rather than assigning them.
